cover.alt: Echo and Leo under the old willow, both touching the glowing blue wish ball

toc.label: Chapter 4: Too Kind for a Fox

text: Leo had a job to do. He had to hold very still.
Brindle was napping on his mane. Brindle napped there most days. A lion’s mane makes a good pillow.
Echo sat on a log with his sly grin.
“Look at you, Fuzz,” said Echo. “Lion life is so easy. You just sit there and look cute.”

media.alt: Brindle naps on Leo’s fluffy mane while Echo grins at them from a log

text: “It is not easy,” said Leo softly. He did not want to wake Brindle. “Fox life is easy. You nap all day and tell jokes.”
“My jokes are good,” said Echo. “You have one joke. You tell it all day.”
Leo grinned. “What did the big rock say to the little rock?”
“Don’t,” said Echo.
“Nothing! Rocks can’t talk!”
Leo laughed so hard that Brindle woke up.

media.alt: Leo laughs at his own joke, Brindle wakes up with a jump, and Echo covers his eyes

text: Brindle gave a big yawn. He went off to nap in the sun.
“Come on,” said Leo. “Let’s go for a walk. I will show you the old willow.”
They went past the stream. They went past the frog rock. At the far end of the Hollow stood a willow tree.
It was very old. Its long, thin branches hung down to the grass. They looked like a yellow curtain.

media.alt: Leo and Echo walk toward a huge old willow tree whose long yellow branches hang down to the grass

text: Leo and Echo went in under the branches. It was still and hushed in there, like a secret room.
The wind went swish, swish in the leaves.
Leo held up his wish ball. “Will it glow?” he said. He said that each time. It hardly ever did.
Echo rolled his eyes. “Okay, wish ball,” he said. “I wish I was a big, cute lion. Then I could nap all day.”
“And I wish I was a fox,” said Leo. “Then I could be sly and quick.”

media.alt: Inside the willow’s curtain of branches, Leo holds up his wish ball as Echo rolls his eyes

text: They both put a paw on the ball. It began to glow. Blue, then bluer, then BLUE!
SWISH went the willow. FLASH went the ball.
Echo felt big. Very, very big. He looked down. He had huge gold paws and a fluffy mane.
“Uh-oh,” said Echo. The words came out big and deep, just like Leo.
Next to him sat a fox with a green satchel. The fox looked down at its black legs and white tail tip.
“Uh-oh,” said the fox. It was Leo.

media.alt: A big blue flash lights up the willow as Echo and Leo swap bodies

text: Echo looked at Leo. Leo looked at Echo.
“You are ME!” they both yelled.
“Wish it back!” said Leo. “Wish it back, quick!”
They put their paws on the ball. They wished and wished. They wished so hard, their ears went pink.
The ball did not glow. Not one bit.
“Great,” said Echo. “Just great.”

media.alt: Echo, now in Leo’s body, and Leo, now in Echo’s body, both press on the wish ball, which will not glow

text: Just then, a song came from the top of the willow.
“Breaking news! Breaking news!” It was Wren. “Did I just hear a FLASH?”
“You can’t hear a flash,” said Echo, from inside Leo.
“Hmm,” said Wren. She looked at them. They both did big, fake grins.
“Boring!” sang Wren. And off she went to find better news.

media.alt: Wren peeks down from the top of the willow while the swapped Echo and Leo do big fake grins

text: Echo let out a big breath. “No one can know,” he said. “If Wren finds out, the whole Hollow will know by lunch.”
“So it is a secret,” said Leo. “Then we have to be each other. Just until we swap back.”
They shook on it. Leo’s paw was tiny now. Echo’s paw was as big as a pumpkin.
“To be me, you have to be kind,” said Leo. “Say please and thank you. Help all of them. And tell my rock joke.”
“Ugh,” said Echo.

media.alt: The swapped friends shake on it: a huge lion paw and a tiny fox paw

text: “To be me, you have to be sly,” said Echo. “Give all of them a nickname. Smirk a lot. And when there is work, pretend to nap.”
“What is a smirk?” said Leo.
Echo showed him, on Leo’s big lion face. It looked like a sneeze was coming.
Then Leo had a go, on Echo’s fox face. It looked like a sneeze was coming there too.
They both burst out in a laugh. Then they went home to be each other.

media.alt: Echo in Leo’s body shows Leo in Echo’s body how to smirk, and it looks like a sneeze

text: Echo went back to the big oak. It was hard work to be so big.
He bumped his head on a branch. He stepped on his own tail. He sat on a bush, and the bush went flat.
Tansy ran up to him. “Leo! Leo! I lost my map! Now I will never find my acorns! Will you help me?”
Echo wanted to say, “Nope.” But Leo would help.
“Um… please,” said Echo. “And thank you. Yes.”
Tansy stared at him. “Why did you say thank you?”

media.alt: Echo, in Leo’s big body, has squashed a bush flat as Tansy runs up asking for help

text: At noon, Tansy came back with a big heap of grass.
“Here you go, Leo! Your best lunch! The long, sweet grass from the stream!”
Foxes do not eat grass. But Leo did. So Echo took a bite. He chewed and chewed. He chewed some more.
“Mmm,” said Echo, with a very green look on his face. “Yum. So very… green.”
When Tansy looked away, he hid the rest in his mane.

media.alt: Echo, in Leo’s body, chews a mouthful of grass with a sour face while Tansy smiles proudly

text: Next came the mouse twins. Pebble had her brush. She got the burrs out of Leo’s mane each day.
Brush, brush, brush. It was SO itchy.
“Hee! Ha! Stop!” yelled Echo. “That is too funny!”
A big clump of grass fell out of his mane.
Pebble stared. “Leo does not yell when I brush him.”
“He does too,” said Pip.
“He does not!” said Pebble.
The twins went home, still fussing. Echo let out a breath. That was close.

media.alt: Pebble brushes the mane of Echo, in Leo’s body, as a clump of grass falls out and Pip looks on

text: Then Brindle came back for his nap. He flopped down on the mane. In a second, he was snoring.
Echo had to hold still. Very, very still.
A fly landed on his nose. He held still.
His leg went to sleep. He held still.
“Leo’s job is hard,” Echo said to himself. “He is kind all day, and he never gets to move.”

media.alt: Brindle snores on the mane of Echo, in Leo’s body, who holds very still with a fly on his nose

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Too Kind for a Fox

text: Leo was having a hard day too.
Fox legs are very quick. Leo took one step, and ZOOM! He shot off like a rocket.
He zoomed past Tansy. He zoomed past the stream. He zoomed into a bush.
In the bush was Moss. Moss did what Moss always does. He rolled into a ball.
“Oh no! I am so sorry!” said Leo.
Moss peeked out. “Echo said sorry?” he said, in a small squeak.

media.alt: Leo, in Echo’s quick fox body, zooms into a bush and Moss rolls into a ball

text: Leo had to think fast. Echo gave all of them a nickname.
“Um… hello, Sweet Pea,” Leo said to Moss. Moss rolled back up.
Then Leo saw Tansy. “Hi there, Sunshine!”
Then he saw Puddle. “Hello, Honey Bun!”
Tansy’s mouth fell open. “Echo just said I was his Sunshine,” she said. “Is he sick?”
Puddle did not hear a thing. He was looking at a moth.

media.alt: Leo, in Echo’s body, waves too sweetly at Tansy, whose mouth falls open, while Puddle watches a moth

text: Leo went to sit on a log. He looked in Echo’s green satchel.
In it was a feather. There was a shiny button, a bit of string and six acorns.
And at the very bottom, there was a map, scratched on bark.
It was Tansy’s lost map! Echo had found it, and he did not tell a soul.
Leo grinned. “Echo is kind too,” he said. “He just hides it.”

media.alt: Leo, in Echo’s body, finds Tansy’s bark map at the bottom of Echo’s satchel

text: Leo ran to give Tansy her map. He only crashed into two bushes on the way.
Tansy hugged the map. Then she hugged the fox. “Echo, you are the best!”
Leo wanted to say, “You are welcome, Sunshine!” But he did not. Echo would smirk and say nothing.
So Leo did his best smirk. It still looked like a sneeze.
“Hiding a kind thing is hard,” he said to himself. “It is like a sneeze you have to hold in.”

media.alt: Tansy hugs her map and the fox, as Leo, in Echo’s body, does his best sneezy smirk

text: At dusk, the two met back at the willow.
“I want my mane back,” said Leo.
“I want my legs back,” said Echo. “And I never want to eat grass again.”
First, they wished on the ball. It did not glow.
Then Echo said, “In stories, you bonk heads. Then you swap back.”
So they bonked heads. BONK!
“Ow,” said Leo. “Ow,” said Echo. They were still swapped.

media.alt: At dusk by the willow, the swapped friends bonk heads with a BONK

text: “Let’s spin three times and say the wish backwards,” said Leo.
They spun one, two, three times. “Me was I wish I!” they yelled.
The Hollow went round and round. Echo tipped one way. Leo tipped the other way.
SPLASH! They both fell in the stream.
Puddle came paddling by. “Oh, hello,” he said. “Is this a bath? What was I doing?”
They were wet. And they were still swapped.

media.alt: The dizzy friends splash into the stream as Puddle paddles past

text: Then Wren zoomed in. “BREAKING NEWS! BREAKING NEWS!” The whole Hollow came running.
“Leo ate grass and made a yuck face!” sang Wren. “Echo said please! Echo said SORRY! I think Leo and Echo swapped!”
The whole Hollow laughed. “Oh, Wren,” said Tansy. “You mix up all your news.”
“Do I?” said Wren.
“Yes,” said Pip and Pebble. “You still mix up US.”
Echo and Leo did not say a word.

media.alt: Wren sings her breaking news, but Tansy and the mouse twins just laugh, while the swapped friends keep still

text: When the rest went home, Moss stayed. He came up very slowly.
“I know,” he said softly. “Leo does not smirk. Echo does not say sorry. I will not tell.”
Then Moss looked at the wish ball. “When you swapped, were you grumpy?”
“A bit,” said Echo.
“Then it was a grumpy wish,” said Moss. “Maybe the ball wants a real one.”

media.alt: Moss comes up slowly and whispers to the swapped friends under the willow at dusk

text: Echo looked at Leo. It was hard to say, but he said it.
“Your job is hard, Fuzz. You are kind all day. The whole Hollow needs you.”
Leo looked at Echo. “Your job is hard too. You do kind things, and then you hide them. You found Tansy’s map.”
Echo went red. But you could not tell under all that fur.
They put their paws on the ball. “I wish I was me again,” they said.
And this time, they meant it.

media.alt: The two friends put their paws on the wish ball together under the willow

text: The ball began to glow. Blue, then bluer, then BLUE!
SWISH went the willow. FLASH went the ball.
Echo looked down. Thin black legs! A white tail tip! His green satchel!
Leo looked down. Big gold paws! A big, fluffy mane! His wish ball!
Leo gave Echo a huge hug.
“Thank you,” said Echo. Then he smirked. “I mean… nice mane, Fuzz.”

media.alt: A blue flash under the willow, and Echo and Leo are back in their own bodies, hugging

text: They walked home in the dusk.
“What did the big rock say to the little rock?” said Leo.
Echo let out a long breath. “Nothing,” he said. “Rocks can’t talk.”
And then Echo laughed. Not a fake laugh. A real one.
Moss did not say a thing. He just smiled.
Back at the far end of the Hollow, the willow went swish. Swish. It had a secret too.

media.alt: Echo and Leo walk home under the first stars, laughing, with Moss smiling behind them
